Sarah —

Appreciate the note. Attached is an initial TAM coverage matrix and our standard escalation map. High level answers here first, and Marissa (CS lead) and Karthik (solutions) are cc'd for any technical clarifications.

- Support hours / SLAs: 24/7 P1 coverage for Dedicated customers with a 15-minute acknowledgement SLA, target time-to-recovery dependent on incident class (we provide target MTTR bands: Critical 1–4 hours, Major 4–24 hours, Minor next-business-day). Full definitions are in the PDF attachment.
- TAM contacts: Primary TAM is named in the matrix (team-level contact + 1:1 TAM rotation). Backup escalation goes to the global TAM oncall pool; critical incidents escalate to the Head of Customer Success.
- Escalation SLAs: Acknowledgement (15 min P1, 1 hour P2), Initial remediation plan within 1 hour for P1, 4 hours for P2.
- Incident comms: Initial notification within 15 minutes (P1), status updates every 30–60 minutes until mitigation, and a post-incident report within 72 hours. We include a standard initial notification template in the worksheet.

Attachment stubs: [Attachment: Redwood_TAM_Coverage_Matrix_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)], [Attachment: Escalation_Map_CF-2039.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)].

If those pieces look OK, Marissa will tailor the one-page matrix for inclusion in your RFP pack and we can add further supporting evidence (SOC2 excerpt, audit log samples) if required.

Hi Sarah —

Quick follow-up with a short, RFP-ready summary inline and some optional choices Cobalt can select:

1) Coverage model (choose one):
   - Standard Dedicated (recommended): 24/7 P1, standard TAM work-hours (Mon–Fri 9–6 local) + oncall for incidents.
   - Enhanced TAM (add-on): Dedicated TAM coverage 08–20 local + named backup TAM, proactive weekly reviews, monthly risk sessions.

2) Escalation path (one-page):
   - Level 1: Customer TAM -> Redwood oncall engineer (ack within 15m)
   - Level 2: Escalation to TAM manager and Solutions Architect (action plan in 1h)
   - Level 3: Head of CS / VP eng (executive notifications and priority resourcing)

3) Templates & cadence: initial P1 notice, 30-min status updates until stabilised, 24‑hour exec summary, 72-hour postmortem.

I'm attaching a simplified one-page matrix for you to drop into the RFP. If you'd like, we can also provide a redacted postmortem from a previous customer showing our communication cadence (requires NDA).

Sarah —

Quick technical confirmation to address the committee questions:

- Named backup TAMs: for Enhanced TAM we supply a contractually acknowledged named backup (person + contact) for the first 6 months; after that we maintain a named rotation with 30 days' notice on changes. We can add explicit language to the SOW.
- Level 3 triggers: automatic escalation when an incident meets either (a) Severity = Critical and time-to-recovery > 4 hours, or (b) Customer requests executive engagement at any time. We'll include the two trigger bullets in the sample clause.
- SLA clause sample (for procurement): "Redwood shall provide 24x7 monitoring and P1 acknowledgement within fifteen (15) minutes. For P1 incidents, Redwood shall use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate and restore service, with target MTTR of 1–4 hours depending on incident class; where remedial actions require third-party cloud provider intervention, Redwood's target shall be extended to reflect provider timelines and Redwood will provide hourly updates until resolved."

I'll prepare the exact contract snippet and a one-page escalation map for insertion into your RFP packet. Please route the NDA to procurement@cobaltfinancial.com and we'll send the redacted postmortem under that agreement.

Thanks,
